summary_html: Court orders a **service plan or supervision** period following a substantiated finding. The goal is rehabilitation and reunification consistent with federal 'reasonable-efforts' requirements.
authority_html:

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The Court reversed the Appellate Division and reinstated termination, holding that the Division's reunification efforts are measured by their adequacy in the circumstances, not by whether they succeeded.
key_cases.relevance: D.M.H. defines the 'diligent efforts' the Division must make under a court-ordered service plan.
key_cases.quote: These efforts must be assessed against the standard of adequacy in light of all the circumstances of a given case.

key_cases.case_name: Division of Youth & Family Services v. G.M.
key_cases.holding: The Court held that after a Title 9 abuse-or-neglect finding the parent is entitled to a dispositional hearing on whether the children may safely be returned, and remanded because none was held.
key_cases.relevance: G.M. frames the court's authority to order services and supervision at disposition following a finding.
key_cases.quote: upon a finding of abuse and neglect, the offending parent or guardian is entitled to a dispositional hearing

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Department of Children & Families v. I.S.
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a Title 9 action must be dismissed when no abuse or neglect is proved, but that jurisdiction may continue where the Division also proceeds under Title 30 to secure needed services for the child.
key_cases.relevance: I.S. identifies N.J.S.A. 30:4C-12 as the route for court-ordered services where no abuse or neglect finding exists.
key_cases.quote: when the Division brings its complaint also under the authority granted to it under Title 30, the court's jurisdiction may continue

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. A.G.
key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination of the rights of parents with serious mental illness, holding the Law Against Discrimination does not supply a defense in a termination case although the Division must still make reasonable efforts accommodating a parent's disability.
key_cases.relevance: A.G. holds that court-ordered service plans must account for a parent's disability even though the LAD is no defense.
key_cases.quote: reliance upon the LAD is misplaced in the context of a termination of parental rights case

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. F.M.
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed the termination of a mother's parental rights, holding that substantial and credible evidence supported each of the four best-interests prongs, including that her inability to shield the children from their dangerous father satisfied prongs one and two and that the Division's enumerated services satisfied the reasonable-efforts prong.
key_cases.relevance: F.M. measures the adequacy of a court-ordered service plan by the steps the Division actually took toward reunification, not by whether they succeeded.
key_cases.quote: Ultimately, a child has a right to live in a stable, nurturing environment and to have the psychological security that his most deeply formed attachments will not be shattered.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. A.R.G.
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed as modified and remanded for de novo reconsideration, holding that 'aggravated circumstances' excusing the Division from reasonable reunification efforts under N.J.S.A. 30:4C-11.3 is a fact-specific inquiry and that a parent must first receive notice of the underlying facts and theory the State will rely on.
key_cases.relevance: A.R.G. defines the narrow circumstances in which a court may relieve the Division of its statutory duty to provide reunification services, and what notice the parent is owed first.
key_cases.quote: Moreover, any circumstances that increase the severity of the abuse or neglect, or add to its injurious consequences, equates to "aggravated circumstances."

state_agency.name: New Jersey Division of Child Protection and Permanency

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: Hearing on the next court day (the Division must cause a complaint to be filed within two court days after the removal, N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.30(b))
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child's emergency (“Dodd”) removal from the home without a court order
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: If there has been no hearing on the removal at which the parent or guardian was present or had an adequate opportunity to be present, the parent or guardian may apply for a hearing on returning the child, which must be held within three court days of the application except for good cause shown (N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.32).

notice_requirements.timing: At least 24 hours before the court hearing (reasonable effort by the Division)

statutory_basis.citation_text: N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.30(a) (the Division shall make a reasonable effort, at least 24 hours prior to the court hearing, to notify the parent or guardian of the time to appear in court and to inform the parent or guardian of the right to obtain counsel, and how to obtain counsel through the Office of the Public Defender if indigent)
